$doc: The floating chat pill's appearance, as data — the source of the `@component ask-fab` block's GENERATED CORE in css/components.css and of dist/react/ask-fab.tsx. ASK-FAB IS THE FIRST SPLIT BLOCK, and that is the fact worth knowing before reading it: everything here renders into a generated region, and two rules of the same block stay authored below it under their own `authored:ask-fab — unnamed-condition` marker. They are `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` and `@media print`, and the reason they stay is the reason the census names — a condition this system cannot name. `$conditions` holds VIEWPORTS, each named for the number it carries; a reduced-motion preference and a print surface are not viewports and have no number, so naming them there would put two things into one list that answer different questions, and `@media {name}` would stop meaning `a width`. The block is therefore accounted for twice over: the core is byte-compared against a fresh render, the remainder declares a reason the scan finds in it, and nothing between the two is unaccounted. See design-system/PATTERNS.md for the third shape and scripts/build.mjs's census for the form.

block.title: Ask FAB (floating chat pill)
note: The chat action's mobile form. Below 700px Ask leaves the docked bar for
the bottom-right corner — where messages are expected — as a floating
pill: the assistant's face at 2rem (a portrait's first step up from the
bar's 1.25rem mark) plus the full label. Past the top of the page the
label folds away and a circle with the face is what remains; js/fab.js
toggles `data-collapsed` and nothing else, so CSS owns the fold the same
way it owns every other state here.
THE BLUE IS THE GROUND, exactly as it is in the bar — the owner's call,
reversing an earlier version that dressed the pill in chrome with the
accent as a ring around the face. That version optimised for quietness,
and quiet was the wrong brief: this is the page's ONE primary action and
the only route to the assistant on a phone, and a solid brand-coloured
bubble is what a decade of chat widgets has taught readers to look for.
The system's own rule says it plainly — the primary action wears the
accent — and it should not stop being true at 699px.
No hairline, matching `.bar__action` (the bar's accent segment draws no
border either); the 2px offset shadow STAYS, because that shadow is what
makes a floating object one of this site's printed things rather than a
generic material FAB. Hover commits to the ink, same as the bar: blue at
rest is an invitation, ink is what it looks like once you are in it.
It replaces the theme puck at this corner; the puck's mobile home is the
menu sheet. Same z tier as the puck had: under the menu (300) and the
drawer (400), so an open sheet covers it.

rules.$doc: The pill at rest: a fixed object in the bottom-right corner, hidden until the viewport is narrow enough for the rule under it to show it. `display: none` in the base and `flex` under the condition is the honest order — the desktop case is the default and the phone is the exception, which is the same way round as the bar it replaces.

note: 2px, not a space token: it is a rim, not a padding step — the face fills
the pill to within a hairline of blue, the owner's call. The right side
keeps a real step so the label can breathe.

rules.$doc: MOBILE ONLY, and the number is the one the bar gives up at. 699 rather than 700 because the bar's own query claims 700 and above; the two are one decision written from both sides, which is exactly the drift a named condition closes — `below-699` is consumed here and by nav, and neither block can move it alone.

rules.name: hover
rules.$doc: Hover commits to the ink, same as the bar: blue at rest is an invitation, ink is what it looks like once you are in it. The 1px lift is the shadow's, not the pill's — the offset shadow stays put and the object rises off it.

rules.name: face
rules.$doc: The assistant's portrait, filling the pill. A part rather than a variant because it is a second element inside the button, and it is the only thing left once the label folds.

note: 2.75rem: the 48px pill minus the 2px rim on each side. The face IS the
pill now — at 44px the drawing reads as a portrait outright, and the
blue survives as the rim, the label's ground and the collapsed ring.

rules.name: label
note: The fold: max-width, not display — a label that vanishes in one frame
reads as a glitch, one that folds reads as the pill closing. 12rem is a
ceiling comfortably past the label's real width; the transition's visible
speed is set by the distance, so keep the ceiling honest if the label
changes.
rules.$doc: The words. Its note is a RULE note rather than a group note because it explains the whole rule — the choice of max-width, the ceiling, and what sets the speed — and the stylesheet writes it above the selector, which is the distinction the two note keys record.

rules.name: collapsed
rules.$doc: The folded pill: the rim on all four sides and no gap, so what is left is a circle the width of the face. An ATTRIBUTE state — js/fab.js toggles `data-collapsed` and writes nothing else, so the fold is CSS's the same way `:hover` is. It is the first suffix in the vocabulary that is a data attribute rather than a pseudo-class, and pipeline 2 renders it as the arbitrary variant `[&[data-collapsed]]:` for the reason `:hover` is rendered arbitrarily: a shorter class that compiles to a different selector is not a transcription.

rules.name: label-folded
rules.$doc: The label, folded away. Scoped to the STATE rather than given a modifier, which is the shape only a named reference can reach — `.ask-fab[data-collapsed]` owns no selector an author could quote, and this is the third block to need that (media's `.ph:has(img) .ph__label` and drawer's sheet are the others). The accessible name does not fold with it: it is an `aria-label` on the button and spec.md is where that rule lives.

THE TAIL THIS BLOCK IS FAMOUS FOR, now said in the definition rather than only in the stylesheet. Two rules follow — `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, which stops the pill's transitions, and `@media print`, which removes it — and both are conditions this system deliberately will not name, because `$conditions` holds VIEWPORTS and each is named for the number it carries. A reduced-motion preference and a sheet of paper have no number. When ask-fab was the only split block the remainder needed no declaration here: there was one hole, it was at the end, and the marker in the CSS was the whole record. `menu` put a hole in the MIDDLE, so a gap became a rule in the list — and adopting it here costs no bytes and makes the census two-sided for this block too: the reason is now claimed in one place and proved in the other.
